title: Focaccia genovese
intro: Thin, oily and salty, with dimples full of brine: soft inside and golden on top.

steps.t: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the water, add the flour and mix; add the salt and 2 tbsp of oil and knead for 10 minutes.
Cover and let it rise for 1 hour at room temperature.
steps.label: Rise

steps.t: Oil a 30x40 cm baking pan well, lay the dough in it and stretch it gently with your fingers.
Let it relax for 20 minutes: if you pull it now, it springs back.
steps.label: Relax

steps.t: Stretch it to the edges, cover and let it rise for another hour.
steps.label: In the pan

steps.t: Meanwhile, beat the brine water, the remaining oil and the coarse salt with a fork.
Pour half the brine over the dough and press your fingertips down to the pan to make dimples; pour over the rest.
Let it rise for 45 minutes: the dimples should stay full of brine. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 230 °C.
steps.label: Final rise

steps.t: Bake on the lowest rack for 18-20 minutes, until golden on top but still soft.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Take it out, brush with a little oil and let it cool slightly on a rack.

tips.t: In Genoa it's eaten for breakfast, even dunked in cappuccino.
Top it with thinly sliced red onions for focaccia with onions.
Next day, warm it for 5 minutes at 200 °C: crisp outside, soft inside again.

title: No-knead bread
intro: No kneading and an overnight rest: a crackling crust and an open, airy crumb.

steps.t: In a bowl, mix the flour, salt and yeast; pour in the water and stir with a spoon for 1 minute, until no dry flour remains.
Cover with plastic wrap and leave at room temperature overnight, 12-18 hours: the dough should be full of bubbles.
Turn it out onto a surface dusted with semolina, fold it over itself 3-4 times and shape into a ball.
Place it seam side down on a floured towel, cover and let it rise for 2 hours.
steps.label: Rise

steps.t: Meanwhile, for the last 30 minutes, heat a lidded cast-iron pot in the oven at 240 °C.
Tip the loaf into the hot pot, cover and bake for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Covered

steps.t: Remove the lid and bake 15 more minutes, until the crust is deep brown and sounds hollow when tapped underneath.
steps.label: Uncovered

steps.t: Let it cool on a rack for at least 1 hour before slicing: it's still cooking inside.
steps.label: Cool

tips.t: The hot lidded pot traps steam: that's what gives the crust its crackle.
Swap 150 g of the flour for whole wheat and add 80 g of chopped walnuts.
From day three, toast it for bruschetta or blitz it into breadcrumbs.

title: Piadina romagnola
intro: Flour, lard and a scorching pan: the soft, tender flatbread of Romagna.

steps.t: Mix the flour, salt and baking soda; add the lard in small pieces and rub it in with your fingers until it disappears.
Add the water a little at a time and knead for 5-8 minutes, until smooth and firm.
Wrap in plastic and let it rest for 30 minutes so it rolls out without shrinking.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Divide into 4 balls and roll them out to 25 cm discs, 3 mm thick.
Heat a cast-iron pan or griddle well over medium-high heat, with no fat.
Cook each piadina for 2 minutes per side, popping bubbles with a fork, until spotted golden.
steps.label: Cook

steps.t: Keep them warm wrapped in a towel, fill them right away and fold in half.

tips.t: Classic with squacquerone cheese and arugula, or prosciutto; in winter with sausage and onions.
For a vegan version, use 70 ml of extra virgin olive oil instead of the lard.
Keeps 2 days in a bag; warm it in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side.

title: Grissini torinesi
intro: Hand-stretched breadsticks from Turin: crisp, rustic and uneven in the best way.

steps.t: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the water, add the flour and oil, then the salt; knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Shape the dough into a 2 cm thick rectangle on a semolina-dusted surface, brush with oil and cover.
Let it rise for 1 hour 30 minutes, until puffy.
steps.label: Rise

steps.t: Heat the oven to 210 °C (conventional). Cut the dough into 1.5 cm strips with a knife or bench scraper.
Take each strip by both ends and stretch it, pulling and shaking, to the length of the baking sheet.
Lay them on a lined baking sheet, a finger's width apart.
Bake for 15-18 minutes, until golden and crisp; bake one sheet at a time.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let them cool on the sheet: they'll get even crisper.
steps.label: Cool

tips.t: Wrapped in prosciutto, or dipped in bagna cauda, they're Piedmont's aperitivo.
Before baking, sprinkle with sesame seeds, chopped rosemary or smoked paprika.
In a tin box, they stay crisp for a week.

title: Naan
intro: India's yogurt flatbread, soft and blistered, cooked in a blazing pan like in a tandoor.

steps.t: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the lukewarm water and wait 10 minutes, until foamy.
steps.label: Yeast

steps.t: Add the flour, salt, yogurt and oil and knead for 6-8 minutes, until soft and smooth.
Cover and let it rise for 1 hour 30 minutes, until doubled.
steps.label: Rise

steps.t: Meanwhile, melt the butter with the very finely chopped garlic and set aside.

oven.t: Meanwhile, heat the oven to max (250 °C) with a pizza stone or tray inside, and melt the butter with the garlic.

steps.t: Divide the dough into 6 balls and stretch them into teardrops 4 mm thick, with oiled hands or a rolling pin.
Heat a cast-iron pan over high heat and cook one naan for 1-2 minutes, until bubbly and charred in spots underneath.
steps.label: First side

oven.t: Bake on the hot stone with the broiler on for 3-4 minutes, until puffed and charred in spots.

steps.t: Flip it and cook for 1 more minute.
steps.label: Second side

oven.t: No need to flip it: take it out as soon as the top is spotted too.

steps.t: Brush right away with the garlic butter, sprinkle with cilantro and keep warm in a towel.

tips.t: Perfect with dal, chicken tikka masala or palak paneer, to mop up the sauce.
Tuck a spoonful of grated cheese into each ball and seal it before rolling for cheese naan.
Press a few nigella seeds onto the surface before cooking.

title: Pão de queijo, cheese bread
intro: Tapioca and cheese puffs, crisp outside and chewy inside.

steps.t: Bring the milk, oil and salt to a boil in a small pan.
Pour it boiling over the starch and stir with a spoon until crumbly; let it cool down.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Add the egg and knead by hand until smooth, then the cheese: the dough is sticky but holds its shape.
With oiled hands, roll 3 cm balls and space them on a lined baking tray. Heat the oven to 180 °C.
Bake until puffed and lightly golden: crisp outside, soft and stretchy inside.
steps.label: Bake

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 170 °C for 15 minutes in a single layer, well spaced.

steps.t: Serve them right away while hot, when they're at their best.

tips.t: Swap half the starch for polvilho azedo from a Brazilian shop for the original tangy flavor.
Freeze them raw on a tray, then bag them: bake from frozen at 180 °C for 30 minutes.

title: Khobz, Moroccan bread
intro: Flat round loaf with semolina and anise, soft inside, torn by hand at the table.

steps.t: Mix the flour, semolina, yeast, sugar, anise and salt. Add the water and oil and knead for 10 minutes, until smooth and soft.
Divide the dough into 2 balls, cover and let them rest.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Flatten each ball into a 20 cm disc, 2 cm thick, on a tray dusted with semolina. Cover and let rise until puffy.
steps.label: Rise

steps.t: Meanwhile heat the oven to 220 °C.
Prick the loaves with a fork, brush with water and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake at 220 °C for 20 minutes, until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Cool wrapped in a tea towel so the crust stays soft.

tips.t: Cut it into wedges and use it to scoop up zaalouk and tagine sauces.
Semolina gives the dense crumb and typical aroma: don't swap it for another flour.
Toast leftovers in a pan and serve for breakfast with olive oil and honey.

title: Skillet cornbread
intro: Southern cornbread baked in a hot cast-iron skillet: crisp crust, moist crumb.

steps.t: Put a 25 cm cast-iron skillet, or a metal cake pan, in the oven and heat to 220 °C so it gets very hot.
steps.label: Skillet

steps.t: Meanwhile, mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and sugar in a bowl.
In another bowl, beat the eggs, yogurt and milk: this stands in for buttermilk.
Take out the hot skillet with an oven glove, melt the butter in it and pour two thirds into the egg mixture.
Fold the wet mix into the dry with a few strokes: a few lumps are fine, don't overmix.
Pour the batter into the hot skillet, it should sizzle, and bake until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it rest for a few minutes, then cut into wedges and serve warm with butter or honey.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Butter in a screaming-hot skillet makes the crisp crust: don't skip preheating the pan.
In the Deep South many make it with no sugar or wheat flour, just cornmeal: more rustic.
Great next to chili, fried chicken or a hot soup such as clam chowder.
